texts.preamble: )Sh. Sandeep Sudhan vs Sh. Hukum Singh on 1 April, 2019 :: 1 :: In The Court Of Ms.Poonam A. Bamba District & Sessions Judge, New Delhi Fsat No. 16/2018 1.)Sh. Sandeep Sudhan S/o Om Prakash Sudhan 1340, Qutab Road, Delhi110006. R/o 23B, Plot No.2 Rohtak Road, New Delhi110005. 2.)M/s Kanhiya Lal Kishori Lal 1340, Qutab Road, Delhi110006.
texts.facts: Vide this appeal, the appellant has challenged the order dated 06.09.2018 of Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (New Delhi), Delhi ("ADM" in short) directing the appellants no. 1 & 2 (partner of the supplier firm and the firm) to pay a consolidated penalty of Rs.30,000/ and appellants no.3 & 4 (director & nominee, respectively of manufacturing company) to pay a consolidated penalty of Rs.60,000/ under Section 52 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 ("FSS Act" in short) for violation of Sections 26(2)(ii), 23(1) & 27(3)(c) read with Section 3(1)(zf)(c)(i) of FSS Act and Regulation 2.2.2.2(f)(i) of The Food Safety and Standards(Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011 ("FSS(P&L) Regulations" in short) for selling misbranded food. Briefly stating, the facts which are not in dispute are that: (i) on 29.05.2017, a sample of "Mix Fruit Jam" was purchased by the Food Safety Officer ('FSO' in short) from Sh.Vinod Saini s/o Late Sh.Bansi Ram, Food Business Operator of M/s The Leela Palace, New Delhi situated at Diplomatic Enclave, New Delhi110023, where the said food article was found stored for serving to the customers/for human consumption; (ii) the sample consisted of four sealed jars of "Mixed Fruit Jam"; each jar containing 1kg taken as such in original condition bearing identical label declaration; (iii) the sample was divided into four equal parts by converting one sealed jar of "Mixed Fruit Jam" as one counterpart of the sample. One counter part of the sample was sent to the Food Analyst for examination. The Food Business Operator did not request to send the fourth part of the sample for analysis from NABL accredited laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of The Food Safety and Standards Rules,2011(FSSR). In view of the same, the two counterparts of the sample in a sealed packet as well Mr.Sandeep Sudhan & Ors. vs State, FSO Page No.3 of 15 :: 4 :: as the fourth counterpart in a separate packet were deposited with the Designated Officer on 30.05.2017; (iv) the Food Analyst vide his report dated 07.06.2017 found that percentage of ingredients used i.e. mix fruits was not declared on the label although, it is emphasised as present, on the label through pictures; and therefore,the sample is misbranded because there is violation of regulation no.2.2.2.2(f)(i) of FSS(P&L) Regulations; ) Sh. Sandeep Sudhan vs Sh. Hukum Singh on 1 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79777500/ 2 (v) on the basis of the above report, a complaint against the appellant was filed before the Ld.ADM. Notice of the same was issued to the appellant and hearing was given. The Ld. ADM after hearing both the sides passed the impugned order. 3.0 The appellant has challenged the impugned order on the following grounds: (i) the Ld. ADM failed to appreciate that the mixed fruit jam is a standardized product and was not being sold as mixture or combination of foods; label of standardized products are not required to declare the percentage of ingredients. Hence , Regulation 2.2.2.2(f) Mr.Sandeep Sudhan & Ors. vs State, FSO Page No.4 of 15 :: 5 :: (i) of FSS(P&L) Regulations was not applicable to the sample food article. The only requirement for the standardized food article/ mixed fruit jam is to give the names or ingredients as per 2.2.2.2(b) of FSS(P&L) Regulations; (ii) Section 32 FSS Act mandates that prosecution should not be initiated for minor defects like the labelling defect in the instant case. Despite being informed that the alleged violation, though not made out, has been rectified, the Ld.ADM proceeded with prosecution and imposed the penalty; (iii) the Ld.ADM failed to appreciate that defence under Section 80(B)(2)(a)(d)(e) FSS Act was available to the appellants no.1 & 2 in view of the fact that the sample food article was sold in the same condition as purchased from the manufacturer company M/s Vidya Sagar Food Pvt. Ltd.vide valid invoices; and it was purchased by the FSO during inspection on 29.05.2017 in the same sealed condition, in which it was purchased by the FBO/ M/s The Leela Palace. But, the Ld. ADM without appreciating the same, proceeded to pass the Mr.Sandeep Sudhan & Ors. vs State, FSO Page No.5 of 15 :: 6 :: impugned order; (iv) the Ld. ADM failed to appreciate that Delhi Food Laboratory in which the sample was analyzed and analytical report was given, is not a legally competent lab to analyze the sample food article as per Section 43 FSS Act; it is neither NABL Accredited nor notified in Official Gazette as per provisions Section 3(1)(p) FSS Act; (v) report of Food Analyst is not admissible as per provisions of FSS Act unless proved by the Food Analyst. Because it is not conclusive (as per Evidence Act) unlike under PFA Act 1954; (vi) penalty has been imposed for violation of Regulations No. 2.2.2.3 & 2.2.2.10 of FSS(P&L) Regulations although, neither was violation of said provisions reported in Food Analyst's Report nor was the complaint filed for violation of the same; )Sh. Sandeep Sudhan vs Sh. Hukum Singh on 1 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79777500/ 3 In view of the same, imposition of penalty on the director and nominee of the said company i.e. appellants no.3&4 is illegal. Reliance in this respect is placed upon the judgment of Delhi High Court in MCD vs Kishan Chand and another dated 25.03.1975 in Criminal Appeal No.122/72. 4.0 On the other hand, Ld.Chief Public Prosecutor for the State sought dismissal of this appeal with heavy cost. It was submitted that during the proceedings before the Ld.ADM, the appellants themselves pleaded that they have now corrected the deficiency in the label and even placed on record, the subsequent package/label after correction. Same shows admission on their part of non compliance of Regulation 2.2.2.2(f)(i) of FSS(P&L) Regulations. The said violation amounted to mis branding in terms of Section 3(1)(zf)(c)(i) FSS Act. Section 52 FSS Act prescribes a penalty of upto Rs.Three Lacs for sale etc. of misbranded food. But, the Ld.ADM imposed a consolidated penalty of only Rs.30,000/ on appellants no. 1 & 2 and a consolidated penalty of only Rs.60,000/ on appellants no.3 & 4. 5.0
texts.arguments: In addition to the General Labelling requirements specified in 2.2.1 above every package of food shall carry the following information on the label, namely,-- ..... 2. List of Ingredients: Except for single ingredient foods, a list of ingredients shall be declared on the label in the following manner: -- ..... (b) The name of Ingredients used in the product shall be listed in descending order of their composition by weight or volume, as the case may be, at the time of its manufacture; ..... ) 4 (f) Every package of food sold as a mixture or combination shall disclose the percentage of the ingredient used at the time of the manufacture of the food (including compound ingredients or categories of ingredients),if such ingredient- (i) is emphasised as present on the label through words or pictures or graphics; or" 6.1 7.0 It would be pertinent to mention here that Section 23(1) FSS Act requires that no one shall manufacture, distribute, sell any packaged food products which is not labelled as per regulations. Section 23(1) reads as under: "23. Packaging and labelling of foods.(1) No person shall manufacture, distribute, sell or expose for sale or despatch or deliver to any agent or broker for the Mr.Sandeep Sudhan & Ors. vs State, FSO Page No.9 of 15 :: 10 :: purpose of sale, any packaged food products which are not marked and labelled in the manner as may be specified by regulations: Provided that the labels shall not contain any statement, claim, design or device which is false or misleading in any particular concerning the food products contained in the package or concerning the quantity or the nutritive value implying medicinal or therapeutic claims or in relation to the place of origin of the said food products." 7.1 Further,such noncompliance renders a packaged food article misbranded in terms of Section 3(1)(zf)(c)(i) of FSS Act. )Sh. Sandeep Sudhan vs Sh. Hukum Singh on 1 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79777500/ 5 7.2 Section 26(2)(ii) FSS Act casts a responsibility on FBO not to sell misbranded food article. Said provision reads as under: 26.Responsibilities of the Food business operator. ..... (2) No food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture, store, sell or distribute any article of food - ..... (ii)which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter; or" 7.2.1 Section 27(3)(c) FSS Act fastens liability for sale etc. of Mr.Sandeep Sudhan & Ors. vs State, FSO Page No.10 of 15 :: 11 :: misbranded food article. Said provision reads as under: "27. Liability of the Manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers. ..... (3)The seller shall be liable under this Act, for any article of food which is ..... (c)misbranded; or" 7.2.2 8.1 Let me refer here to Section 80(B)(2) of FSS Act, under which the benefit of defence is sought. Same reads as under : "80. Defences which may or may not be allowed in prosecution under this Act. (A)... Mr.Sandeep Sudhan & Ors. vs State, FSO Page No.11 of 15 :: 12 :: (B) Defence of due diligence (1)... (2) Without limiting the ways in which a person may satisfy the requirements of clause (1), a person satisfies those requirements if it is proved: )Sh. Sandeep Sudhan vs Sh. Hukum Singh on 1 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79777500/ 6 (a) that the commission of the offence was due to -- (i) an act or default of another person; or (ii) reliance on information supplied by another person; and (b) (i) the person carried out all such checks of the food concerned as were reasonable in all the circumstances; or (ii) it was reasonable in all the circumstances to rely on checks carried out by the person who supplied such food to the person; and (c) that the person did not import the food into the jurisdiction from another country; and (d) in the case of an offence involving the sale of food, that-- (i) the person sold the food in the same condition as and when the person purchased it, or (ii) the person sold the food in a different condition to that in which the person purchased it, but that the difference did not result in any contravention of this Act or the rules and regulations made thereunder, and (e) that the person did not know and had no reason to suspect at the time of commission of the alleged offence that the person's act or omission would constitute an offence under the relevant section. 8.1.1
